historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (13.0-13.5%) diverges >30% from the 3-yr revenue CAGR (6.8%). Equity is not a clean growth gauge here: it compounds retained earnings net of ~$1B/yr buybacks and was depressed by the COVID loss year. Revenue 3-yr CAGR is used as the growth anchor; the 5-yr revenue CAGR (12.7%) and 5-yr EPS CAGR are distorted by the COVID base (CSV FY2021 revenue 12.5B, EPS $0.24), so EPS 5-yr is left null.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): CSV FY2021 1,734.2; FY2023 835.7; FY2024 1,368.0; FY2025 1,245.6; FY2026 1,859.5. The 3-yr figure (30.6%) starts from the FY2023 inventory/freight-cost trough and the 5-yr (1.4%) from the COVID working-capital release, so neither is a forward rate. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR runs ~2pp ABOVE reported FCF because interest income fell as rates eased and cash was used to repay notes - not because SBC is shrinking; SBC grew 13%/yr (121.9 -> 175.4) but is under 1% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 surge (+10% traffic-led comps in Q2, op margin +205bp ex the tariff refund) is real but partly a trade-down spike; comps normalise to 2-3% against tough compares from FY2027 and Ross compounds on ~3% annual unit growth toward 2,900 Ross / 700 dd's stores. Tariffs turn roughly neutral entering FY2027 as China-plus-one sourcing (Vietnam, India, Malaysia) matures, and operating margin settles at ~13.5% - the pre-COVID band - with no e-commerce cost drag. Capex peaks at ~$1.1B this year and fades. Capital return continues (~$1.3B buybacks/yr) but is value-neutral in this model.
scenario_narratives.bull: Conroy's merchandising reset and a structurally richer close-out supply (department-store and specialty retail distress) keep comps at 3-4% for several years while dd's DISCOUNTS reaccelerates unit growth; Ross closes part of its margin gap to TJX's Marmaxx (~14.5% mature) as freight, packaway and DC efficiencies compound and tariff mitigation leaves AUR increases sticking. Revenue grows 7-8%/yr mid-decade and the store runway lasts longer.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 proves the peak: once the tariff refund and the trade-down traffic wave pass, comps go flat in FY2027 (lapping +10%), China-heavy sourcing leaves Ross exposed to renewed tariff escalation, and TJX and Burlington's aggressive store openings compete away prime off-price real estate and close-out supply. Operating margin falls back to the 11.5% of FY2024-25; a US-only, store-only model has no international or online hedge, and the leadership transition after a 40-year incumbent adds execution risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ross is a mature, net-cash, store-growth compounder: value is a steady owner-FCF stream with modest unit growth, so a 10-year component build at a 9% USD cost of capital with an 18x (base) terminal cap is appropriate. SBC is small (<1% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow; the valuation turns on the durable operating margin (11.5% vs 13.5% vs 14.5%) and on how much of FY2026's comp surge persists.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 is flattered by a ~$253M one-time IEEPA tariff refund and a +10% traffic-led comp that may be a trade-down spike
High China-sourcing exposure: renewed tariff escalation would hit margin before mitigation
Close-out supply depends on full-price retail overproducing; tighter vendor inventory discipline starves the model
TJX and Burlington store expansion competing for real estate and goods
New CEO (Feb 2025) after a 40-year incumbent; strategy changes untested through a downturn
US-only, no e-commerce: no hedge against US consumer or policy shocks

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 147.49-257.00
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 745732): 10-K FY ended 2026-01-31 and 10-Q Q2 FY2026 (period ended 2026-08-01, shares on cover 2026-08-14); ROST_Metrics.csv for history
data_sources.qualitative: ROST_Analysis.json (Q2 FY2026 results, raised FY2026 guidance EPS $8.61-$8.77 incl ~$0.60 tariff refund, ~115 new stores, ~$1.1B capex, ~$1.275B buybacks)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted estimate: 319.45M basic shares on the Q2 FY2026 10-Q cover (2026-08-14) plus ~1.0M unvested restricted stock/PSU dilution (Q2 diluted weighted average 319.45M while the count was falling ~1.3M/quarter from buybacks). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY ended 2026-01-31 cash-flow add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation 175.354M). Ross publishes no adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation and no separate PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag; withholding on vesting is small and runs through the repurchase line, so the add-back is used alone (slight understatement of the true SBC cost).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.95 for a defensive-ish off-price retailer -> cost of equity ~9.0%. Net cash balance sheet, so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: straight-line rent (~$843M FY0 operating lease cost) sits inside cost of sales/SG&A, so EBITDA and the flows are already after rent. Operating lease liabilities ($3.69B at 2026-01-31) are therefore NOT added to net debt. One treatment: lease cost in the flows, never also in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1/2: profitable US operating retailer; no REIT/bank/holdco features; no prior DCF and no MEMORY entry, so this is a fresh build). PERIOD LABELS: this folder's CSV labels a fiscal year by the calendar year it ends in, so CSV FY2026 = Ross 'fiscal 2025' (ended 2026-01-31) = FY0 here; Year 1 of the projection = Ross 'fiscal 2026' (ends ~2027-01-30), the year management guides EPS $8.61-$8.77. CSV quarterly labels are also shifted (CSV 'Q2 2027' = Ross Q1 FY2026 to 2026-05-02; 'Q3 2027' = Q2 FY2026 to 2026-08-01) and the CSV's quarterly balance-sheet rows sit one quarter late - anchors here were taken from SEC XBRL companyfacts by period-end date, not from the CSV labels. ANCHORS: cash $4,288.1M and debt $1,018.5M ($241.5M current + $777.1M non-current senior notes) at 2026-08-01 (Q2 10-Q) -> net cash $3,269.6M; the CSV's latest balance sheet (2026-01-31: cash 4,594 / debt 2,017 incl. the since-repaid notes) is stale. OWNER FCF FY0: OCF 3,026.9 - capex 819.3 = 2,207.6 reported; less SBC 175.4 and interest income 172.7 (net cash > 1x FCF base) = 1,859.5. FY0 OCF was flattered by working capital (OCF +28% vs NI +3%), so the projection does not start from it: the engine rebuilds year 1 from components. BUYBACKS: a real repurchaser - $1,050M in each of the last two years, $637.5M in H1 FY2026, ~$1.275B planned for FY2026 under the $2.55B authorisation to Jan-2028 - so the flat share count is funded, not a convention. Buybacks run well ahead of SBC (~6x), which is capital return on top of the flat-count convention and is value-neutral in this model. YEAR 1 includes the ~$253M one-time IEEPA tariff refund (~1.0pp of op margin, ~$0.60/share) because it is real cash received; it is removed from year 2 onward. Year-1 operating margin ~13.7% (12.7% underlying) ties to the low end of the $8.61-$8.77 EPS guide: op income ~$3.51B + ~$125M net interest, 24.5% tax, ~319M shares.

bear.ebitda_margin_path_note: Op margin 13.3 (H2 misses guide) -> 11.8 -> 11.6 -> 11.5 mature: the FY2024-25 level, i.e. the H1 FY2026 margin step-up proves to be a cyclical/trade-down spike plus one-off refund.

base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA = GAAP operating margin + D&A% + SBC%. Op margin path: 13.7 (FY2026 incl. ~1.0pp tariff refund; 12.7 underlying) -> 13.0 -> 13.2 -> 13.3 -> 13.4 -> 13.5 mature, back to the pre-COVID 13-14% band as tariffs turn neutral and freight/packaway efficiencies hold.
base.growth_rates_note: Year 1 = H1 actual +16.7% plus H2 guided comps +4-7% and ~115 new stores (~+9% H2) -> ~+12.5%. Then ~3% unit growth (toward 2,900 Ross / 700 dd's) plus 2-3% comps, fading to 3% as the store runway matures.
base.capex_pct_path_note: FY2026 guided ~$1.1B (~4.3%) on new stores, supply chain and IT; glides to ~3% as the DC build-out completes, staying above D&A while units grow.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: GAAP ETR 24.5% FY0 (697/2,842); cash taxes paid ran lower (21%) on timing, not a carryforward, so the GAAP rate is used.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Inventory-led retailer: growth absorbs a little working capital net of payables (packaway inventory), so capture is modestly negative.

bull.ebitda_margin_path_note: Op margin 14.0 -> 13.6 -> 14.0 -> 14.3 -> 14.5 mature (above the FY2019 peak) on merchandising gains under Conroy and full tariff mitigation.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default) because the stock is pricing a year that is flattered by a one-off refund and an unusually strong traffic surge, and tariff policy is a live single-regulator risk; balance sheet carries no solvency risk, so not higher. Base 55% because management's long-run unit plan and pre-COVID margin band are well evidenced. Bull 25% (below the 35% default) because it needs comps, margin expansion past the FY2019 peak, and a longer store runway to all go right together under a new CEO.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
